title: Strict-tower equivalence and projection-normalized Roos comparison for a clopen cover
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $I$ be a finite set, and let $j_i:X_i\hookrightarrow X$ be pairwise disjoint open and closed immersions whose images cover $X$ [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Use the small pro-etale sites in the fixed universes [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and their unbounded derived categories and cochain complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

For a sheaf of commutative rings $R$ on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ put $R_i=R|_{X_i}$ and let $r_i$ be restriction. A strict tower is a sequence of complexes $C_n$ of $R$-modules with chain maps $t_n:C_{n+1}\to C_n$; its morphisms are families of chain maps commuting with $t_n$ [def-weil-inverse-system]. Restriction is an equivalence from strict $R$-module towers to tuples of strict $R_i$-module towers. Its inverse has
$$G((C_{i,n})_i)^m_n(U)=\prod_i C_{i,n}^m(U\times_X X_i),$$
with componentwise differentials, transitions, module actions and tower maps. The equivalence's unit is restriction of sections and its counit is projection to the component.

Put $P_C=\prod_n C_n$ termwise, with projections $\operatorname{pr}_n$, and let $v_C=1-s_C$ have $n$th coordinate $\operatorname{pr}_n-t_n\operatorname{pr}_{n+1}$ [def-weil-tower-transition-endomorphism]. The canonical comparisons
$$\alpha_{i,C}:r_iP_C\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_n r_iC_n$$
commute with differentials and every projection and satisfy $\alpha_{i,C}r_i(v_C)=v_{r_iC}\alpha_{i,C}$. For gluing, the corresponding comparison is the reindexing $\prod_n\prod_i C_{i,n}^m(U\times_X X_i)\cong\prod_i\prod_n C_{i,n}^m(U\times_X X_i)$ fixing each $(i,n)$ coordinate.

Use $H(C)=\operatorname{Cone}(v_C)[-1]$ [def-weil-strict-roos-model] with $H(C)^m=P_C^{m-1}\oplus P_C^m$ and $d(y,x)=(-dy-v_Cx,dx)$. There is a chain isomorphism $r_iH(C)\cong H(r_iC)$ equal to $\alpha_{i,C}$ on both summands. It is natural for strict tower maps, which act diagonally by $\prod_n f_n$. It preserves the cone projection $(y,x)\mapsto x$, its composites with every $\operatorname{pr}_n$, and the connecting map $z\mapsto(-z,0)$ to the shifted cone, with this signed convention. Localization gives an isomorphism in $D(R_i)$ with these same map identities. The termwise products represent derived products. A specified triangle $K\to P_C\xrightarrow{v_C}P_C\to K[1]$ is distinguished if and only if all its component triangles are distinguished [def-weil-derived-limit], retaining the specified first and connecting maps under the product and shift identifications. These assertions include the empty partition: then $X$ is empty and all categories, towers and triangles are zero.

proof.text: Import the extracted exact restriction data and proved product, normalized module-gluing and generic Roos support lemmas [lem-pur-clopen-strict-tower-roos-core]. Public data retain their original names and definitions. Private compatibility wrappers retain the original signatures used here and by import-all consumers. The remaining strict-tower and derived-triangle proofs are unchanged. This is a compilation split after profiling and definition/interface simplification, not a change of the mathematical route.

Apply [lem-pur-clopen-ringed-module-gluing] degreewise and at each tower level. For a tuple of towers, define $G$ on differentials, transitions and morphisms by its componentwise module formula. Functoriality gives $d^2=0$, $dt=td$ and the strict-map equations in [def-weil-inverse-system]. Naturality of the gluing unit and counit applied to each differential and transition makes them isomorphisms of strict towers. Their degreewise inverses also commute with these maps. Thus they exhibit the asserted equivalence, with exactly the displayed section formula and unit/counit. No replacement of a tower by an objectwise isomorphic diagram is needed.

proof.text: Use the forgetful functor to additive presheaves to show that open restriction preserves countable products: sectionwise precomposition preserves them and the forgetful functor reflects them. Evaluation of module sheaves and complexes preserves the actual product, giving productSections and its projection equation. Compose these section equivalences with the module-gluing coordinates and transpose the n and i indices. This gives tau with exactly the displayed projection normalization. The transition comparison follows by checking every product projection [def-weil-category-product] and [def-weil-tower-transition-endomorphism].

proof.text: Apply the proved generic additive Roos comparison [lem-pur-roos-comparison-horizontal-coherence]. Its two-summand coordinate formula is the diagonal product comparison. Prove its projection equation by composing that formula with the second biproduct projection. Product projections give the evaluation equation. In the fixed shifted-cone coordinates, boundary is the negative first inclusion; composing the diagonal comparison with that inclusion proves the signed boundary equation. These coordinate computations retain the sign and the actual chain maps [def-weil-strict-roos-model]. Preservation of countable products makes the comparison an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 014E, derived-definition-cone, and Homology Tag 011G, definition-shift-cochain; explicit two-summand computation with the signed map fixed in the statement.

proof.text: Apply any localization functor to the projection, evaluation and signed boundary identities of step 3. Its map_comp equations give the displayed localized identities without choosing a new cone. For triangle reflection, lift the module equivalence of [lem-pur-clopen-ringed-module-gluing] degreewise to complexes. Exact restriction jointly reflects quasi-isomorphisms by homology. Its inverse preserves quasi-isomorphisms by the counit. The universal property of localization, including localization of the product category, therefore gives an equivalence of derived categories in the exact HasDerivedCategory universe of the statement. The Lean proof reuses the existing generic private helper of [lem-pur-finite-product-derived-tensor-calculus], namely the theorem FiniteClopenTensor.derivedPi_isEquivalence from Sheaf.AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtaleFiniteClopenTensorCalculus via a proof-only import all, applied to the normalized module gluing functors, their zero-map equation, unit and counit, and joint reflection of isomorphisms. Its fully polymorphic binders retain the independent ring, module, index and derived-category universes; no commutative-ring specialization or tensor-calculus theorem is used.

source.place: Tags 05RU, derived-definition-unbounded-derived-category, and 015F, derived-lemma-right-derived-exact-functor; localization of the explicit chain isomorphism.

proof.text: Generalize the proof of exact products [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact] to the independent ring universe used here: an affine weakly contractible covering family [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-affine-wcontractible-covering-family] makes each component epimorphism surjective on sections, hence its countable product is locally surjective. Thus module sheaves satisfy CountableAB4Star. Apply [lem-weil-derived-countable-products-core] to the actual termwise product cone. The canonical localization preserves that cone and its projections. For a restriction functor, use its complex-level preservation of products and its canonical localization comparison; essential surjectivity of Q descends product preservation to the derived restriction. Consequently PreservesProduct.iso has hom equal to the specified piComparison. Verify conjugacy of the tower transition endomorphism after every projection [def-weil-derived-limit].

Exact derived restriction is triangulated [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated], so it preserves distinguished triangles. Conversely complete the first arrow of the specified triangle T to a distinguished triangle S using TR1 [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Every restricted T and S is distinguished, so the identity isomorphisms on the first two vertices extend to a componentwise triangle isomorphism. Full faithfulness of the restriction family, supplied by the derived equivalence of step 4, lifts their third components to an isomorphism in the original category. Faithfulness and the commShift isomorphisms lift the two remaining triangle equations. Thus T is isomorphic to S and distinguished. Finally conjugate the two product vertices by the projection-normalized product isomorphisms of step 5. Their transition equation and the explicit shifted last arrow give exactly the IsDerivedLimitTriangle equivalence, with no replacement of its specified arrows [def-weil-derived-limit]. The calculation of product-transition conjugacy and the three triangle equations is proved once in the private generic helper limit_triangle_descent over abstract triangulated categories, then specialized to the derived restrictions; it introduces no new hypothesis or postponed proof.

For an empty partition the covering hypothesis forces X empty. The empty-cover sheaf axiom forces every section of every module sheaf to be zero. Hence every module, strict tower and complex is zero. Essential surjectivity of the canonical localization makes every derived object zero too. Each category is equivalent to Discrete PUnit since all hom sets are singletons. The specified triangle is isomorphic to the contractible zero triangle, hence distinguished by TR1 [def-weil-triangulated-category]. This also verifies the empty-partition edge case without any nonzero or nonemptiness assumption.
